rv.q: The wonder is that it took so long. After enduring cruel punishments such as the Take That and Spice Girls musicals, at last we have a jukebox musical to sing about. Roddy Doyle's delightful 1987 novel is made up mostly of dialogue, so perfect for dramatisation- and it's all about music.

The biggest compliment I can pay Jamie Lloyd's production is to say that it really has got soul. It's memorably gritty at times (the swear-word count is exceptionally high) and also proves wonderfully funny and touching. This is much more than a bogstandard compilation musical.
Jimmy Rabbitte (Denis Grindel) is the ambitious would-be manager who gathers the members of what he calls 'the hardest-working band in the world'.

But, on the face of it, the stage would appear to be the natural destination for this material. The storyline provides a castiron excuse for storming through a string ofclassic soul and Motown numbers - "In the Midnight Hour", "What Becomes of the Broken-Hearted", "Satisfaction" et al :- without toppling into the dreaded "jukebox musical" category.

The songs are belted out with gusto, the cast is terrific and the dialogue has plenty of salty zing. Ever since Roddy Doyle wrote It's quite a ride; the trouble is, it The Commitments in 1987 and doesn't really go anywhere.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Palace Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.
Farther from the stage than center orchestra — less up-close, but the sound still carries well.
At 1,648 seats, Palace Theatre is one of the larger Broadway houses — far side mezzanine seats sit well off-axis and a long way from the stage.

vs.sum: Spectacularly renovated in a $100M+ project that literally raised the theater 30 feet. The restoration preserved its opulent 1913 interior while upgrading acoustics, seating comfort, and best-in-class restrooms on every level — widely considered the best facilities on Broadway.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Wheelchair, aisle transfer, and companion seating on all levels.
